events.event: Bisnis.com summarises karhutla spread and government mitigation: Health Ministry counts 283,270 acute respiratory infection cases since August, and police plan to deploy 70,000 forest police.
events.key_numbers: ARI cases 283,270 (Aug-13 Oct) in 7 provinces, 63 regencies/cities · ~63,700 children aged 0-5 · 12 regions in hazardous air category · 2,458 flights disrupted at 29 airports (11 Aug-17 Oct, +437 vs 13 Oct) · 70,000 forest police planned · 5,179 water-bombing flight cycles by 38 aircraft · ~500 peat hydrological units to be mapped
events.why_it_matters: Haze now has a measurable health toll: hundreds of thousands of breathing infections, including many small children.

events.event: BMKG says dry conditions will continue 17-24 Oct and reports 478 high-confidence hotspots on 16 Oct, led by South Sumatra, with Central Kalimantan down sharply from 15 Oct.
events.key_numbers: 478 high-confidence hotspots (16 Oct) · South Sumatra 189 · East Java 89 · South Papua 63 · West Kalimantan 26 · Central Kalimantan 26 (from 485 on 15 Oct) · dry outlook 17-24 Oct
events.why_it_matters: The dry spell through 24 Oct means haze and flight disruptions are unlikely to end soon.

events.event: Palangka Raya extends its karhutla emergency status to 9 Nov after 909 fire incidents since 1 June.
events.key_numbers: 909 incidents (1 Jun-17 Oct) · 1,448.90 ha burned · emergency status to 9 Nov · Way Kambas fire burning since 15 Sep (25 hotspots inside park, Lampung 84 total)
events.why_it_matters: Local emergency status shows the haze is a months-long crisis in Kalimantan, not a passing event.
